entry.title: A ring off, a ring on
entry.summary: The books describe taking rings off a post before finding a way to put them back. Repeating one small movement can be the whole activity, with adult supervision, materials suitable for mouthing, appropriate sizes and secure parts.
entry.cue: Your child may enjoy lifting off a ring, turning it, or finding the post again.
detail: The Baby appendix begins its rocking-base example once a baby can sit stably, around 8–11 months. Its stable-base example is listed at 8–12+ months, depending on skill with the earlier activity. A large opening gives the hand room to find the post.

Later Baby examples use a basket with two or three rings and a peg at 10–12+ months, then two or three same-size napkin rings on a spindle at 11–12+ months. These offer different ways to repeat taking off and putting on; they are not a shopping list.

Both appendices list four or five rings of different sizes from 12+ months. The Baby chapter also describes horizontal and curved posts; the Toddler appendix places those variants around 14–16 months, and three colored pegs with rings at 15–18+ months.
The Baby authors separately consider finishes suitable for tasting and chewing, the size of each object and its components, and secure attachments without choking hazards.

A child may put rings on any colored peg before becoming interested in matching. The books leave room to adjust the number of pieces, offer help, or come back another day. Color matching and a completed stack are not the point of every turn.

ageContext.bookAge: Baby: rocking base once sitting stably, around 8–11 months; stable base 8–12+ depending on prior skill. Later materials have their own age labels.
ageContext.readiness: A comfortable position the child has reached independently, interest in the hand movement, and materials suited to the child, with adult supervision.
ageContext.note: An earlier material can still offer a satisfying hand movement. Matching or grading need not become a test.

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
displayContext.colophon: Original summaries inspired by The Montessori Baby and The Montessori Toddler. Open any idea for its book references. The illustration is an invitation to explore, rather than a room to reproduce. Follow your child’s pace.
